**Finding: MISSING — no insurance clause (severity: low)**

**What I found**

A full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and reading all 75 paragraphs confirmed the gap. Section 14 (General Provisions, p0063–p0073) covers governing law, publicity, independent contractor status, fees, notices, severability, force majeure, assignment and counterparts — then goes straight to the signature block. There is no insurance covenant anywhere, and no exhibits are attached to the filed document.

**Why it matters here**

Two features of this deal make the omission worth fixing rather than waiving:

- **Kubient processes our data.** Section 9(b)(iii) (p0035) has Kubient warranting the security of its "collection, maintenance, management and storage of visitor information (data)." That is the trigger for cyber cover under the rule, and a data-processing vendor with no insurance sits squarely in walk-away territory.
- **The indemnities have no financial backstop.** Section 10(a) (p0047–p0051) gives us broad indemnification covering the Services, the Auction Platform and third-party Creative — meaningful exposure for an ad-tech intermediary. Combined with the mutual consequential-damages waiver in Section 7(a) (p0027), recovery depends entirely on Kubient's own balance sheet.

**The edit**

One new subsection (j) inserted after p0073, inside the existing General Provisions section — the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position, with no renumbering of existing clauses. It requires CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber/privacy of USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, additional-insured status on the CGL policy limited to Kubient's indemnity obligations, and certificates on request.

Two points of drafting judgment worth flagging: I tied the cyber cover to "visitor information (data) and Customer's Confidential Information" rather than to "Customer Data," since that term is not defined in this agreement and the quoted phrasing tracks Section 9(b)(iii) and Section 12. I also scoped the additional-insured request to Kubient's indemnification obligations, which is easier for a vendor's broker to accept than an open-ended endorsement. The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment so Kubient can move without a second round.
